title: Affirmative and Negative Sentences
description: Learn to form negative sentences and double negatives in Spanish, plus affirmative equivalents.

grammar.title: Basic Negation with No
grammar.content:
Forming negative sentences in Spanish:

Basic negation:
No quiero ir. (I don't want to go.)
No tengo dinero. (I don't have money.)
No estoy cansado. (I'm not tired.)

Double negation (required in Spanish):
No hay nadie. (There is nobody.)
No veo nada. (I don't see anything.)
No voy a ninguna parte. (I'm not going anywhere.)

Negative words that require 'no' in affirmative sentences:
Nunca he estado en Paris. (I've never been in Paris.) → No negative word before verb needed
Pero: with negation, BOTH must be present:
No he estado nunca en Paris. (I have never been in Paris.) — more emphatic

Key negative words:
- nunca (never)
- jamais (never, more emphatic)
- nadie (no one)
- nada (nothing)
- ninguno/ninguna (none)
- ni...ni (neither...nor)
- ni siquiera (not even)
examples: No quiero nada. (I don't want anything.)
No hay nadie en casa. (There's nobody home.)
No tengo ningun problema. (I don't have any problem.)
Nunca me lo dijo. (He never told me.) / No me lo dijo nunca. (more emphatic)

grammar.title: Double Negatives in Spanish
grammar.content:
In Spanish, TWO negatives are often used together for emphasis:

No hay nadie = There is nobody
No veo nada = I don't see anything
No voy a ningun lado = I'm not going anywhere

Double negative with 'ni':
No tengo ni tiempo ni dinero. (I have neither time nor money.)
No me gusta ni el cafe ni el te. (I like neither coffee nor tea.)

Using 'ni' alone (without preceding 'no'):
Ni lo uno ni lo otro. (Neither one nor the other.)
Ni hablar! (No way! / Don't even think about it!)

Other negative expressions:
No importa = It doesn't matter
No tiene importancia = It's not important
No hay de que = You're welcome / It's nothing
No es para tanto = It's not a big deal

Position of negatives:
Negative words can come before or after the verb:
Nunca vienes. / No vienes nunca. (You never come.) — both correct
examples: No tengo ni tiempo ni paciencia. (I have neither time nor patience.)
Ni siquiera me miró. (He didn't even look at me.)
No tengo ningún interés en ir. (I have no interest in going.)
Nunca mais lo hare. (I will never do it again.)

grammar.title: Affirmative and Negative Pairs
grammar.content:
Spanish affirmative ↔ negative pairs:

algún/uno ↔ ninguno
Alguien llamó. → Nadie llamó.

algo ↔ nada
Algo pasó. → Nada pasó.

también ↔ tampoco
Yo también quiero ir. → Yo tampoco quiero ir.

siempre ↔ nunca/jamás
Siempre vengo aquí. → Nunca vengo aquí.

ya ↔ todavía no / aun no
Ya terminé. → Todavía no he terminado.

otro ↔ ningún otro
Otro día será. → Ningún otro día será.

todo ↔ nada
Todo está bien. → Nada está bien.

Both/All ↔ Neither/None:
Todos vinieron. → Ninguno vino.

Expressing agreement/disagreement:
— No me gusta. — A mí tampoco. (Neither do I.)
— Me gusta mucho. — A mí también. (Me too.)
examples: — Quiero ir también. — Yo también quiero ir. / Yo tampoco quiero ir. (I don't want to go either.)
— Siempre llego tarde. — Pues yo nunca llego tarde. (Well I never arrive late.)
— Ya terminé. — Pues yo todavía no he terminado. (Well I haven't finished yet.)
— Todo está bien. — No, nada está bien. (No, nothing is fine.)

pronunciation.title: Negation Pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
Key negative word pronunciation:

no = noh
nada = NAH-dah
nadie = NAH-dyeh (d sounds like 'dy')
ninguno = neen-GOO-noh
ni = nee
nunca = NOON-kah
jamás = hah-MAHS (stress on second syllable)
tampoco = tahm-POH-koh

Contrast with affirmative counterparts:

algo = AL-goh (something)
alguien = AL-gyehn (someone)
alguno = al-GOO-noh (some)

también = tahm-BEEN (also)
siempre = SYEM-preh (always)
ya = yah (already)

Double negative examples:
No hay nadie = noh eye NAH-dyeh (there is no one)
No veo nada = noh BEH-oh NAH-dah (I see nothing)

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'There is nobody' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Spanish requires double negation: 'No hay nadie' = There is nobody. Simply saying 'Hay nadie' is incorrect.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ me gusta el cafe. (I don't like coffee either.)'
exercises.explanation: Tampoco = neither/not either. 'A mi tampoco' = Neither do I / Me neither.

exercises.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
exercises.explanation: Both 'Nunca he estado alli' and 'No he estado nunca alli' are correct. The second is more emphatic.

exercises.question: Complete: 'No tengo ___ tiempo ___ dinero. (I have neither time nor money.)'
exercises.explanation: Ni...ni = neither...nor. 'No tengo ni tiempo ni dinero' = I have neither time nor money.

exercises.question: Which means 'I see nothing' in Spanish?
options: Both B and C are correct
exercises.explanation: Both 'No veo nada' and 'Nada veo' are correct. Position of 'nada' is flexible.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ siquiera lo pense. (I didn't even think about it.)'
exercises.explanation: Ni siquiera = not even. 'Ni siquiera lo pense' = I didn't even think about it.

exercises.question: Which is the affirmative equivalent of 'Nunca' (never)?
exercises.explanation: Siempre = always is the affirmative opposite of nunca = never.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ me gusta. — A mi ___. (I don't like it. — Me neither.)'
exercises.explanation: 'No me gusta' = I don't like it. 'A mi tampoco' = Me neither / Neither do I.

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'No way!' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Ni hablar = No way! / Don't even think about it! (literally: not even to talk)

exercises.question: Complete: 'No tengo ___ interes en ir. (I have no interest in going.)'
exercises.explanation: Ningún = no/not any (contracted form of ninguno). 'Ningún interés' = no interest.
